security.item: A thumbnail is made only from an image file inside the media folders (the Media folders of Joomla and Alfa Commerce's own image folder) whose type matches its extension. Before, a member of staff allowed to edit products, categories or manufacturers, or an API client with that right, could name any file the site can read (a backup, a log, the site's configuration file) as a thumbnail, and a copy of it, its extension kept, was published in the image folder (images/commerce by default) for anyone to download. A save that names such a thumbnail is now refused with a message and writes nothing, so the gallery keeps the thumbnails it had; the API answers 400 with the same reason; the Recreate thumbnails job names an image that breaks the rule in its report instead of copying it.

The update lists the files among the product images that are not images, with the media rows that name them, on the update page and in the media log (com_alfa_media.php in Joomla's log folder). Up to 2.2.0 such a file may be a copy of a site file published by the defect above. Nothing is deleted: look at each file and delete by hand those that are not yours to publish, then choose a new thumbnail for the rows named.

The search, items, easy articles and cart modules answer a request that sends a list where one value is expected (for example module_id[]=1) with "400 Bad Request" and a plain sentence. Before, such a request was answered with an error page that named a file on the server; the search module's address needs no form token.

A registration stores the customer's details exactly as the registration form checked them: each field's own rules and clean-up applied, and nothing kept for a field the form hid. Before, the values were taken from the submitted page as they came, on every account save, Joomla's own registration page included, so a required field could be left empty, a phone number kept unformatted, or a value stored that the form never offered. Details saved before are kept as they are.

A required customer details or registration field whose form field plugin is disabled, missing, or not available to the visitor (its Access is not Public) now stops the form with a message naming the field, instead of being left out and the order, account or details saved without it. This covers every form that asks for those fields: the checkout, the registration form, the customer's My details page, and the customer details and order forms staff use. An optional field in that state is left out, as before, and noted in the log. A new row of the setup checklist names each required field that not every visitor can fill in, with the details it is required in.

A request to the component's storefront pages or to its REST API that sends a list where one value is expected (for example id_line[]=1) is answered "400 Bad Request" with a plain sentence. Before, some storefront pages answered with an error page that named a file on the server.

Issuing a sales document now needs the Sales Documents: Create permission and voiding one the Sales Documents: Change State permission, checked by the document service itself whoever calls it. The screens and the API already asked for them; an extension that issues or voids documents is now held to the same rule. Automatic issue on a status change is the shop's own policy and asks no staff permission.

A request to the component's administrator screens and their tasks that sends a list where one value is expected (for example id[]=1) is answered "400 Bad Request" with a plain sentence, as the storefront and the REST API are. Before, some answered with an error page that named a file on the server. It needs a signed-in administrator.

With Joomla's System - Page Cache plugin on and System - Alfa Commerce Sync disabled, not installed or set to an Access that visitors who are not logged in do not hold, a visitor's cart page, with the checkout details typed and the coupon, and the cart module on every page were stored and shown to the next visitors. The cart page in every form (the cart, the checkout, the empty cart and the order pages), the cart module while it shows products, and every page priced in a currency or place of the visitor's own now keep themselves out of the page cache whatever plugin is enabled. A page whose cart module is empty stays cacheable.

fix.item: A registration refused by its checks (two passwords that differ, for example) is no longer shown to other visitors: with Joomla's System - Page Cache plugin on, the registration page re-filled with the name, username and e-mail typed was stored and shown to the next visitor who opened the registration page, with the password typed in its form. The page now keeps itself out of the page cache, the password typed is no longer kept at all, and the other fields typed re-fill only the page that shows the refusal, under Alfa Commerce's own session key, so Joomla's own registration page no longer receives them.

A visitor whose session holds a currency or a place of their own, set by a site's own code for Alfa Commerce's prices, is kept out of Joomla's System - Page Cache: every page priced for that visitor keeps itself out, and System - Alfa Commerce Sync also keeps that visitor from being shown a page stored for another. A listing stored with one visitor's currency was shown to the next visitor with that currency's prices.

The order page shown before payment, reached again by a reload or by Try again, keeps itself out of Joomla's System - Page Cache. With System - Alfa Commerce Sync disabled it could be stored and shown to the next visitor with the order's number.

The items module, showing a visitor's recently viewed products, keeps the page out of Joomla's System - Page Cache. Before, the page stored from one visitor's visit showed that visitor's recently viewed products to the next visitors.

The items module refreshes its best sellers ranking as often as its option says, in minutes: the default 60 refreshes it every hour. Before, it kept the ranking 60 times longer (60 hours by default). An update also clears the module's stored ranking and listings, so nothing the version before computed stays.
REST API: a tax, discount or cart rule that does not exist answers 404, as every other resource does, instead of 500 (GET v1/alfa/taxes/{id}, discounts/{id} and cartrules/{id}).

REST API: a delete that is refused answers 409 with the reason, and nothing is deleted: an order status orders are in, or the last status holding a role, and a payment or shipping method that orders, payments, parcels, stored payment references or a payment method's shipping list still use. It answered 204 while the record stayed. The back office shows the same reason once.

Without the dompdf library (lib_dompdf), which is installed separately, a document's PDF answers 503 with a sentence that names the library, in the back office and over the REST API (GET v1/alfa/documents/{id}/pdf), instead of 500. The setup checklist has a new recommended row, PDF library for sales documents, that says where to get it; status e-mails still go out without the PDF and log it.
REST API: POST v1/alfa/users refuses a Joomla user that does not exist, user 0 and a user who already has a customer record, with the reason (400). The administrator's customer form checks the same.

REST API: a payment or shipping method created without color or bg_color takes the colours its edit screen offers, and a customer group created without prices_display takes the price display Alfa Sync gives every new group; a group updated without it keeps its own. Each failed with a database message.
REST API: a new order status keeps its invoice rules (issues_doc_rules) when the request does not send issues_delivery_note; they were dropped and the status issued no documents.
REST API: PATCH v1/alfa/orders/{id} writes customer_note; it answered 200 and wrote nothing.
Creating an item, a form field, a place or a currency no longer writes PHP warnings to the log.

The stock step of a status change that fails (for example the database was briefly unreachable) is tried again with the shop's usual backoff, and if it keeps failing it shows in Tools > Tasks and in the notification bell. Before, it failed at once and nobody was told, while the order's stock stayed unmoved.

A stock movement that a stock extension refuses on purpose is no longer retried for ever: it is recorded as refused and its notice names the refusal. For an order, staff decide on the order, and a new status that changes the order's stock claim tries it again (a status that keeps the claim does not); for a document, the movement waits in Tools > Tasks, and only running that task again tries it, once the extension allows it. A stock movement that keeps failing for another reason is tried again with the waits the shop's task runner uses (1 minute, 5 minutes, 30 minutes, 2 hours, 6 hours and 24 hours after each failure, about 33 hours in all), then waits for staff and its notice says so; a new status of an order tries that order's failed movement at once, and Apply outstanding stock movements in Tools > Database Sync tries every failed movement at once.

Saving a product is one step: its details, translations, images, prices, categories, manufacturers, who may see it, options, downloads, variants, stock and a move into the archive are all saved, or, if the save stops part way (for example the database was briefly unreachable), none of them is and staff are told that nothing was kept. Before, a save that stopped part way could leave the product with new details and old prices, or with no categories. The catalogue rebuild and the extensions told of the save hear of it only once it is complete. An image removed in the save has its files deleted only once the save is complete, so a save that stops keeps the image and its files; an image uploaded by a save that stops is left in the images folder, where the media maintenance page of Tools lists it under Untracked files on disk.

Saving a discount or a tax rule saves the rule and its scope (categories, manufacturers, places, customers, customer groups) in one step, and extensions told of the save read the scope as it was saved. Before, they were told before the scope was written.

A product or variant price for a country that was later deleted keeps its country: the price editor shows it as "#number (deleted)" with a note, and saving the product unchanged keeps it. Before, the editor showed "All" for such a row and saving the product turned that country's price into a price for every country. Setting such a row to every country is refused, naming the row, and deleting a country that price rows name says so, naming their products.

On a phone, Tools > Tasks, the orders list and an order's page fit the screen. Below 480 px a row of the background jobs list, of the orders list and of an order's payments, shipments, items, documents and reconciliation folds: its values wrap under one another, each named by its column (an extension's column by its own title), and its buttons take a line of their own under it. A background job's next-try date stays on one line. Before, at 360 px the orders list and an order's page were wider than the screen and scrolled sideways (on a test order with one payment and one shipment, 941 px and 1,182 px; in Greek 1,098 px and 1,584 px), and the jobs list's buttons were partly or wholly out of sight, behind a sideways scroll of 14 px in English and 116 px in Greek.

The result of a plugin action, a refused one included, shows its message above its Close or OK button. Before, on a phone, with the site's own messages above it, the button bar pinned to the bottom of the window covered the first lines of the message.

REST API: deleting a currency that orders, prices or places use, or an item field a product still uses, answers 409 with the reason, and nothing is deleted. It answered 204 while the record stayed. The back office shows the same reason once.
REST API: PATCH v1/alfa/orders/{id} with state answers 422 with the reason: an order is not trashed, and its status changes through POST v1/alfa/orders/{id}/status. It answered 200 and wrote nothing.

REST API: a PATCH that leaves out a required name (one that changes only a category's or a manufacturer's state, for example) no longer answers 400 "Field required: Name"; the stored names are kept. A create without a name, and a PATCH that sends the name empty, are still refused.
REST API: the answer to a PATCH of a product's images shows them as saved; it showed them as they were before the save.
A carrier asking for the shipping method of a shipment whose method was deleted, or that has none, is handed nothing, instead of false or an empty new method; a failure reading it is logged.

A price calculation with a quantity list that leaves out one of the products, or gives one a quantity that is not a whole number of at least 1, is refused, naming the product, instead of failing with a PHP error or pricing that product at a quantity of 1 (or 2.5 as 2).

Saving a category tells the search and catalogue plugins about the change after the category's products have been updated and after the save is committed, so a plugin that reads a product then sees the new audience.
A stock allocation plugin is given who placed the order and why, as its interface promises, instead of an empty context; the allocation plugins are collected once per request.

When a plugin's check of an order fails at checkout, the shopper is told which plugin could not check the order, instead of only "Order placement failed"; a plugin that refuses the order on purpose by throwing is read in its own words, as its rejection is.

The notice of a document that could not be issued automatically says why, in the sentence staff read for that refusal when it has one (an order with no currency, for example), else the failure's own first line; a database error is named as one, its detail kept in the log.

E-mail layout overrides are read from the default administrator template whatever sends the mail (the storefront, the REST API, the console), the same template the order status's layout list offers; before, a mail sent from the storefront did not find them.
An order created with a shipping method needs an existing delivery address; one without is refused before anything is written. An order with no shipping method needs none.
Saving a cart rule, a payment method or a shipping method is one transaction, and the plugins told about the save hear it after the commit, with the translations, the conditions and the scope saved.

Updating from 2.1.x no longer warns "The scheduled tasks of plg_task_alfapricesets were not removed": the update removes those tasks itself before it uninstalls the plugin, and says once that the plugin was removed.

The Standard payment plugin's partial refund form offers at most what the order may still refund, so it no longer accepts a figure the refund then refuses (after a credit note settled to the customer's wallet).
A shopper whose order a stock extension refuses at placement reads the extension's own sentence. Before, the shopper read only "Order placement failed", and the reason was in the server log.

A stock movement whose process stopped before it finished (for example it ran out of time or memory) is tried again with the same waits and the same limit as a movement that failed, and after the last try it waits for staff, with the notice that says so. Before, it was tried again every five minutes with no limit.

change.item: The setup checklist has a recommended row, Joomla page cache: it passes while System - Page Cache is off, warns while it runs beside System - Alfa Commerce Sync, saying what Alfa Commerce keeps out of it, what it still stores and that other page caches are not detected, and warns as well while it runs without System - Alfa Commerce Sync, saying that the pages that show a visitor's own data still keep themselves out and that a shopper with products in the cart, or with prices of their own, can be shown a page stored for another visitor. The row is checked again when either plugin is saved or switched from the Plugins list, and when System - Alfa Commerce Sync is enabled again.

System - Alfa Commerce Sync counts only when it runs for visitors who are not logged in: enabled with an Access they do not hold, it is treated as disabled by the page cache row, and the warning on Alfa Commerce's pages says to set its Access to Public.

The warning shown while System - Alfa Commerce Sync is disabled, not installed or set to an Access that visitors who are not logged in do not hold says that the cart, the checkout, the order pages and any page that shows a cart with products still keep themselves out of Joomla's page cache, and what is lost: a shopper with products in the cart, or priced in a currency or place of their own, can be shown a page stored for another visitor, with an empty cart and the shop's own prices. The warning while the plugin is disabled or not installed also names the setup checklist, which no longer updates at once when a payment or shipping plugin is saved or switched.

Options > Downloads has a new switch, Direct-download protection check (Yes by default). With No, the download store's protection is checked only when Check again is pressed, and no page warns about it: the Options say that the check is off and show the last result. Turn it off for a shop that sells no files, or on a server where the site cannot request its own address.

While the download store has nothing to protect (no product carries a file and no order hands one out), no page warns about its protection and nothing checks it; the Options say so. The first file uploaded to the store checks it once.

The warning about the download store's protection is written in plain words: what happened, whether it matters and what to do. The nginx rule is behind a Server rule line under it, and its links open the Downloads tab of the Options, where the store can be moved outside the web root and the check turned off.
REST API: a create (POST v1/alfa/{resource}) answers 201 Created with a Location header naming the new record, instead of 200. The body is the same record as before.

REST API: each payment of an order (GET v1/alfa/orders/{id}) carries added, the time it was recorded, and refund_reason, the reason given for a refund. The field created, which was always empty, is gone from the payments.
REST API: a single order (GET v1/alfa/orders/{id}, and the order answered after a change to it) carries fulfillment_status and fulfillment_percentage, as the orders list does and by the same rule.

For extension developers: DocumentIssuer::issue() takes the actor that issues (a user, or SystemActor for the shop's own policy; the request's identity when none is named) and refuses one without the permission with a DocumentRefusedException, as void() does; an empty void reason is a DocumentRefusedException too. A listener of onInventoryBeforeReserve, onInventoryBeforeCommit or onInventoryBeforeRelease refuses a movement on purpose by throwing InventoryRefusedException with the sentence people are to read: staff for a movement owed after a status change or a document, and, at an order's placement, whoever places the order, the shopper included, so the sentence must be fit for a shopper (no warehouse codes or internal states).

For extension developers: OrderTotalHelper::getShippingTotal() now answers the shipping the order charges after shipping-class cart rules, the figure its total and documents use; before, it answered the carriers' charges before those rules. The carriers' charge is still in OrderTotalHelper::getBreakdown() as shipping_gross_tax_incl.
For extension developers: onAlfaAdminAfterSave for a product, a discount or a tax, and onItemAfterSave, are announced once the whole save has committed, never for a save that was rolled back.

The description of the layout fields (the sub-template choices of a product, a category, a menu item and the Options) says in plain words how to add a version of your own: copy the part's file from the component's folder into your template's override folder and give it a name of your own; it appears in the list the next time the page is opened.

When Alfa Commerce is uninstalled and a language pack has no package manifest, the message says: "This language pack does not include a package manifest." The maintenance log (com_alfa_maintenance.php) names each such pack and why it was not uninstalled.

For template and extension developers: a table in the administrator can fold on a phone with the class alfa-fold (alfa-fold-line for its actions cell, alfa-fold-keep for a heading kept, data-alfa-label for a cell's name), in media/com_alfa/css/admin/admin.css. A list column an extension adds (onAlfaAdminListColumns) carries its title as its cells' data-alfa-label. The class alfa-nowrap-md is replaced by alfa-nowrap (one line at every width). The action page's styles moved from the layouts' inline style blocks into media/com_alfa/css/admin/action-page.css (style asset com_alfa.action-page), which layouts/action/buttons.php and the result screen load.

REST API: a PATCH of a customer group's prices_display changes only the settings it names and keeps the group's others, and a setting it sends empty ("" or null) is removed from the group, which then takes the shop's own setting. A create (POST) that sends an empty prices_display stores no setting of the group's own, so the group takes the shop's settings, where a create that leaves prices_display out gets a copy of them, as before. The customer group's edit screen shows each price display setting as a list, and a setting the group does not hold as "Use Global" with the shop's value; saving keeps it so, and a label setting shows while the shop shows its price. Before, the map sent replaced the stored one whole, a setting sent empty was stored as the field's default, and the edit screen showed a setting the group did not hold as the field's default and saved it as the group's own.

Stock put back on the shelf (an order cancelled or a line cut, a credit note's return) and its reversal (a credit note voided) are announced to stock plugins after the commit, as onInventoryRestored, with what moved by product, variant and location.

For extension developers: a listener of onOrderPlaceValidate may refuse the order by throwing OrderPlaceRefusedException with the sentence the shopper is to read, as reject() does; any other exception it throws refuses the order as a check that could not run.

note.item: Update at a quiet hour if your shop is large. The update rebuilds some tables: five on MariaDB (stock movements, stock operations and the order history get wider record numbers; order lines and parcels longer tax names) and six on MySQL, where the document lines' new tax name column is a rebuild too. While a table is rebuilt, a save that writes to it waits. At the size of a typical busy shop this is a few seconds in all; at ten times that, about 50 seconds in all, up to about 25 seconds for one table.
The update pauses the shop's background work while it runs (at most ten minutes) and resumes it when it finishes.
Clear nothing by hand: the update cleans Joomla's page cache and Alfa Commerce's own caches (the dashboard's cards, the setup checklist, the storefront's category tree and the others) once, itself.

Shops on 2.1 with Joomla's System - Page Cache plugin on: until the update, a visitor who is not logged in can be shown, until the cache time ends, an earlier visitor's cart page (the cart, the coupon, the shipping method, and the name, e-mail and phone typed at checkout), that visitor's cart in the cart module on every other page, and the page a guest buyer reached after ordering. Until you update, turn the plugin off (its exclusion options do not help) and clear Joomla's page cache. The update to 2.2.0 clears Joomla's page cache once, and 2.2.0 keeps those pages out of it.

Update every Alfa Commerce extension you have installed to its 2.2.0 build together with core. With an older build on 2.2.0 an extension loses its dashboard cards, setup checks, tools, document types and panels, and Tools > Extensions answers its Clear Data "not supported".

Payment and shipping plugins that take providers' callbacks need the Access Public (Extensions: Plugins). A provider calls as a guest; a plugin at another Access is not loaded for its callbacks, which are then answered "try again later" and raised as an alert.

The shop's background work no longer needs a cron job: shop pages, staff pages, the notification bell and API requests run it; a server can still run it from cron with the console command alfa:tasks:run. The console commands now come with the plugin "Console - Alfa Commerce"; the update removes "Console - Alfa Inventory" and says so (alfa:inventory:audit keeps its name).

fix.item: Two saves of one product at the same moment, or a save beside a discount, tax or category save, a product list action, a catalogue rebuild or the preparation of a new combination of customer groups, can no longer leave the product's prices, filters or search entry on the older state: each waits for the other (at most ten seconds) instead of being skipped. A product whose catalogue entry could not be rebuilt after it changed (it stayed busy, the database refused, or the request stopped after the change) is remembered and rebuilt by the shop's background work. This covers its save, a name or SKU edited in the product list, its variants, options and info values, the Studio, publishing and unpublishing, and the batch category and manufacturer commands; the background work rebuilds the product's search entry too.

A cart line whose chosen options belong to a product-field extension that is disabled, missing or cannot be loaded is no longer priced without them: it stays in the cart, marked with the reason and without a price, and cannot be ordered until the extension is back or the line is removed. A product with a required field of such an extension cannot be added to the cart, and the shopper is told why. Orders placed before keep their amounts.

change.item: A payment, refund or shipment that moves the order's status now records that move together with the payment, refund or shipment itself, in one save. If the request stops right after the save (a timeout, a closed browser, a server restart), the move is no longer lost: it runs as soon as the shop's background work runs, and the order's e-mail, documents and plugin reactions follow it once. A move that was asked when the order no longer stood where the payment found it (staff or another payment moved it meanwhile) is left out and noted on the order's History; a move the database could not make at that moment because the order was busy is tried again automatically.
The History entries of a payment, refund, chargeback or shipment, new or changed, are saved together with it.
A payment saved again with the same status (for example a gateway that confirms the same payment twice) no longer asks for the order's documents a second time.

A status change records only the follow-up work it really has: no stock step when the stock does not change, no download step for a status that neither grants nor cancels downloads, no documents step for a status that issues none, no e-mail step for a status that tells nobody, and no plugin step when no plugin listens. The settings are read when the status changes. Tools > Tasks lists fewer entries per order; a notice raised twice in one save is one entry.

Work that an order's save leaves for after a gateway's or a carrier's lock, or for after checkout's own steps, is kept for that request from the moment it is saved: the shop's background work no longer picks it up while the request is still busy with it. If the request stops, the background work takes it after 15 minutes.
Updating Alfa Commerce pauses the shop's background work for the length of the update (at most ten minutes) and resumes it when the update finishes.

The stock movement, stock operation and order history tables use wider record numbers, so a busy shop cannot run out of them. The update converts the three tables once; while each is converted, saving to it waits (on a shop the size of the demo, about a second per table; on a shop ten times larger, up to about 25 seconds for one table). Large shops are advised to update at a quiet hour.

The list prices of a new combination of customer groups are now prepared by the shop's own background work, a chunk of products at a time, instead of the scheduled task "Alfa - Prepare list prices for customer groups". The update moves the combinations that wait to it, removes the plugin "Task - Alfa list prices for customer groups" with its scheduled tasks, and says so (a plugin Joomla refuses to uninstall is named in a warning, to remove by hand). Tools > Database Sync shows each waiting combination and how far it is; its button prepares them now.

Tools > Database Sync: "Apply outstanding stock movements", "Rebuild catalogue projections" and "Rebuild search index" now give their work to the shop's background work and follow it under the progress bar until it is done; work that is interrupted goes on from where it stopped. A stock movement left owed (by an order's stock step, or found by the notification bell) is applied by the background work as well.

The shop's background work runs without a cron job: when the shop's pages are visited (one page in 30 seconds asks for it, after it has loaded), when staff use the administrator, from Alfa Commerce's own pages through the notification bell (also while the System - Alfa Commerce Sync plugin is disabled), and after API requests. A server can also run it from cron with the console command alfa:tasks:run, or through a web-cron address with a secret key. The bell and the Dashboard say when work has waited more than a day with nothing run in that time.

The console commands of Alfa Commerce are registered by the new plugin "Console - Alfa Commerce": alfa:tasks:run, alfa:tasks:prune and alfa:inventory:audit, which keeps its name. The update removes the plugin "Console - Alfa Inventory" and says so.

Finished tasks are deleted by the shop's background work, about once an hour, by rules for each kind: done stock, download, document and status-move tasks after 7 days; done e-mails, plugin reactions and jobs after 30 days; resolved tasks 30 days after staff acted. Tasks that failed or are held stay until staff act on them, and the last run of each shop-wide job is kept. When no deletion run has finished for a day, the background work puts the next one ahead of its other maintenance, and the notification bell steps in. Tools > Tasks has "Delete finished tasks now", and alfa:tasks:prune runs for up to 25 seconds; both say how many went.

Each order e-mail that is sent now leaves an entry on the order's History naming each recipient and when it was handed over, saved together with the e-mail's completion, so it remains after the task is deleted. The History entry of an e-mail that failed or is held also names the recipients it had already reached.

Tools > Tasks lists the shop's background jobs: what each covers, how far it is, when it started and finished, and its last error. Process now follows a waiting job to its end on a progress page, which the buttons that rebuild the catalogue projections, apply outstanding stock movements or rebuild the search index now open too. A failed job can be retried or marked resolved with a reason. The tab also shows the last background run, the cron command, and the web-cron address, whose key is shown once, when a new one is generated.

A Tools button pressed again while its job waits or runs no longer just turns grey: the job's progress page opens and says the job is already waiting or running, so nothing new was started. A request that fails says why beside the button, which can be pressed again.

An open administrator page keeps the shop's background work going: while work remains it asks for the next step every 3 seconds, so a job started from Tools (thumbnails, projections, stock movements, the search index) runs to its end with no one clicking again. It stops when nothing is left, while its tab is hidden (and goes on when it is shown), and after 30 minutes without a break; Alfa Commerce's own pages do the same. A shop with no visits and no one in the administrator still needs the cron or the web cron.

Tools > Tasks reads in the order staff act: what needs attention and the run that retries it, the background jobs and the deletion of finished ones, then how the background work runs. It fits a phone, and a job's errors are said in plain words, on a phone too. When the job of a progress page ends, the page says how, prints a thumbnails job's report and draws the list below it again. A new web-cron address and Recreate all thumbnails ask first. A job something is already working reads Running, between two of its steps too, and offers Follow (its progress page); Process now is offered for a job nothing has touched for 30 seconds and for one not started yet. While a job runs or waits, the Dashboard's Background work card shows it with its progress, kept up to date while the Dashboard is open, and opens its page.

Messages, alerts, refusals and the order History name a plugin as Extensions: Plugins does, say whether it is disabled, not installed or could not be loaded, and give times in your own time zone. A refused order delete is one error, never a success message; a payment or shipment whose plugin cannot be used says so in its row; and when a plugin of the customer's cart cannot run for your account, the cart builder disables Place order and says why. An order History entry's Details name its task, its recipients and its plugin in words.
A gallery image's description field says it holds up to 75 characters, and a longer one shortened at save is said to be shortened.

The API reports the shop's background work: GET v1/alfa/tasks/{id}, the list GET v1/alfa/tasks for Tools, and POST v1/alfa/tasks/{id}/process, which works a job for up to 2 seconds and answers 202 with Location and Retry-After while it still waits. A save's answer lists in meta.tasks the jobs it queued, and an order's answer also lists the order's tasks with how each ended. A task its caller may not see answers 404.

The item editor's combinations popups (generate combinations, add options, add informational values, visibility) answer a database refusal with one plain sentence; the details go to the site's log, and the database's own text, its SQL and table names among it, no longer reaches the screen.
The product page's Categories and Manufacturers headings are translated; they showed the English words in every language.

A product with one image shows it in its lightbox with no thumbnail strip and no slider. A product whose variants have galleries of their own loads the gallery scripts for every gallery it can show, so switching a variant from no image or one image to a larger gallery slides it and opens it in the lightbox; it failed with a script error before.

Product page images have meaningful alt texts: a gallery image says the product's name and its number ("Lamp, image 1") unless the merchant gave it an alt of its own; a category or manufacturer image beside its name has an empty alt instead of the name followed by the word logo.
The Alfa Items and Easy Articles modules scope their responsive grid rules to their own panels, so a module of the same kind nested inside one keeps its own layout.

229 language strings are removed from the component's English language files (215 from the administrator's file and 16 from the site's, two of them from both; the Greek pack follows in its 2.2.0 build): 228 that no code uses any more, and COM_ALFA_CART_COUPON_REMOVE from the administrator's file only, whose text stays in the site's file, which the administrator's cart screen loads. With them goes the unused price row form administrator/forms/price.xml, which an update removes.

The API's document lines (GET v1/alfa/documents/{id}) carry a new field, tax_name: the name of the tax rule the line was taxed by, frozen at issue; it is empty on every line of a document issued before 2.2.0.

Printed documents name the tax rules they were taxed by: each row of the tax analysis prints the names of the tax rules of its lines before the rate (for example "VAT 24%"), and two rules at one rate are named together on their row; the column keeps its generic "Tax analysis" label. Each name is the one frozen when the document is issued. A product line names the first tax rule applied to it, the one name its order line keeps, so goods taxed by two rules one after the other show the first only; a shipping charge names every rule applied to it (several joined with +), as frozen when the order was placed; a credit note names what the document it corrects named. Rates print at two decimals, as before. A document never changes after issue, so documents issued before 2.2.0, and the shipping charge of an order placed before it, print the rate alone, as before.

A search engine plugin can tell which result set a shopper saw and where a clicked product stood in it. The catalogue listing's results container carries the engine's handle (data-alfa-search-event) and the order shown (data-alfa-search-order: relevance, or sort:{key}:{direction}), and each product card its place in the whole result set (data-position, counted across pages), only when the engine gave a handle; a listing without one renders none of them. A product card reloaded for a variant keeps its place. The listing's JSON (format=json) carries the same handle, the order and each item's place; the search endpoint's JSON answer carries the handle and the order, a product's place being its index in the products list plus one.

The catalogue listing shows its category's title and description above the subcategories, each by its own new option (Show Category Title, Show Category Description): set per category (Yes, No or Inherit), per Items menu item (Use Global, Yes or No) and globally, both shown by default; a description with nothing in it (an editor's empty paragraph) shows nothing. Joomla's Show Page Heading now works on the listing: the menu item's Page Heading, else its title on the category's own menu item, else the category's name. The page keeps one main heading: under the page heading the category title is a second-level heading. For templates: an override of com_alfa/items/default.php prints none of these until it is updated.

Every public Alfa Commerce event (the administrator's list, form and save events, the menu and permissions events, media, the product page and listing events, orders placed, status changes, stock, catalogue, document and notification events) now reaches every enabled plugin that registered a listener for it, whatever its group, system plugins included, in Joomla's priority order. An event that asks whether something may happen keeps Joomla's rules: a listener that throws stops the operation. An event that reports what already happened, or collects what a page shows, runs each listener on its own: one that fails is logged with its name and the next one still runs, so a broken plugin no longer blanks a screen or silences the plugins after it.

An order's payment and shipping stay with the plugin that took them. The order pages, staff actions, refund reports and the order delete now use the plugin recorded on the order and on each payment or shipment, never the method's current settings. When that plugin is disabled, missing or cannot be loaded: a new order with it is refused before anything is saved; the order pages show a neutral line and change nothing (the process page no longer moves on to the completed page for it); staff actions name the plugin and how to restore it; the refund block holds; and the order cannot be deleted. When the plugin's own part of an order page fails, the process page shows the same neutral line and stays, and the completed page shows without the plugin's part.

A payment provider's or carrier's callback for a plugin that is disabled, missing or cannot be loaded is answered "503 Service Unavailable" with Retry-After, never as received, so the provider tries again; the notification bell raises one alert per plugin with the number of refused callbacks and how to recover. When the plugin is enabled but its Access is a level a provider's request (a guest) does not hold, the alert says so and that the remedy is the plugin's Access (Public for a plugin that takes callbacks); a member of staff whose account lacks a plugin's Access is told the same. The count is exact when callbacks arrive at the same time, and a callback refused after staff closed the alert starts a new alert. A plugin that fails while processing a callback is answered 500.
The plugin of a payment or shipping method can no longer be changed once an order uses the method: the field is read-only with a note, as deleting such a method was already refused.

When staff operate a customer's cart and a plugin that adds a charge or checks the order has an Access the customer holds but the staff account does not, Joomla does not load that plugin for the staff member: the cart builder shows the totals without that plugin's part and says so, and the order cannot be placed from that screen. Give the plugin an Access the staff account holds, or let the customer place the order. An order is never placed with money that differs from the customer's own cart.

A provider's callback for a payment attempt that staff moved to Standard is rejected: the Standard payment is not changed, the rejection is written to the order's history, and one alert is raised per attempt and provider event.

The cart page shows its money in a summary under the products, no longer inside the products table: the subtotal, the tax included, the discount applied, the shipping, each fee, each applied cart rule (a code with its remove button, which names its code) and the total, each row with its name, on phones too. "Clear cart" sits beside the summary on wide screens and under it on phones. On phones every product cell is named in the shop's language, and the quantity cell lines up like the others.
The storefront's shared table rules are now scoped to Alfa Commerce's root (.com-alfa), so a template's own tables on the cart page and the other Alfa Commerce pages are no longer restyled.

The cart page, the cart module and the add-to-cart buttons keep each other up to date: adding a product, changing a quantity, removing a product or clearing the cart on one of them refreshes the others without reloading the page. An empty cart page says when the cart was changed elsewhere and offers to reload.
The cart module's counter grows with its number, so a count of three or more digits stays inside its red pill.

The order-completed page shows the whole order: its number, date and status, the products with their chosen options, the totals as the cart showed them, the delivery and invoice addresses, the shipping and payment methods, the payment state in plain words (paid, partly paid, awaiting payment, refunded), the e-mail the confirmation went to, and a Print button that prints the products, the totals and the addresses. It never shows the phone number, notes, the IP address or payment references. The page now has its own address with the order's key, so reloading it, going back to it or opening it in a second tab shows the same page and repeats nothing; a guest's order opens with its key, a customer's order with its key and that customer logged in. The page is never cached, indexed or sent on in a Referer. Every payment method keeps landing on the page as before.

The update cleans Joomla's page cache and Alfa Commerce's own caches once (the dashboard's cards, the setup checklist, the storefront's category tree and the others), so no page or card stored by the earlier version is served after it; a cache that cannot be cleaned is noted in the maintenance log and the update goes on.

2.2.0 keeps the cart page, and every page of a visitor whose session holds a cart or typed checkout details, out of Joomla's System - Page Cache: such pages are never stored, and such a visitor is never served a stored page, so one visitor's cart or details are never shown to another. Every other page is cached as before.

A saving is stated on the basis of the figures beside it. The cart states every discount tax included, as it states every other figure: a catalogue discount applied before tax shows its tax-included saving on the cart line, in the cart summary and in the administrator's cart screens, and the summary's struck subtotal is what the lines strike (for a product at 200,00 plus 24 percent tax with 5 percent off before tax: a saving of 12,40, not 10,00, and 248,00 struck, not 245,60). The price block of the product page, the product lists, the cart module and the confirmation card shows the saving tax excluded beside its figures before tax (the base price and the subtotal: 10,00) and tax included beside its figures with tax (the price with tax and the final price: 12,40); a block showing both carries each in its place. A saving is shown only beside prices of its own basis: with the base price, the subtotal and the final price shown but not the price with tax, the block shows the saving before tax alone; a block that shows no price (the tax alone) shows the saving tax included, as the storefront states its prices. Nothing is priced differently.

Notifications list: a page now holds as many notices as its limit, only the ones you are allowed to see, and its page count counts only those; the list page shows the notification bell like the other Alfa Commerce lists, and a notice dismissed from the list leaves the bell one fewer.

Deleting a product waits for a save or a price update of that product that is already running, and is refused with a message (nothing deleted) when that takes longer than a few seconds; delete it again a moment later. A delete that cannot remove the product's stored prices is undone whole, so a deleted product's prices are always announced to the plugins that listen for price changes.

When a filter of the filters module changes the products, the page brings the products into view (instantly for visitors who ask for reduced motion) and moves the keyboard focus to them; a later page reached from the pagination opens on its products, and so does a page whose address submits a filter. A first page with no filter opens at its top as before. A template with a sticky header sets --alfa-scroll-offset to that header's height so the products are not hidden under it. A template override of com_alfa/items/default.php keeps this by keeping the results section's data-results and tabindex="-1" attributes and the data-results-reveal mark the view gives it.

Countries and regions that are unpublished are no longer offered in the administrator's place pickers (payment and shipping methods, the Standard carrier's zones, the Country field's settings, prices, discounts and taxes), nor is a place inside an unpublished country. A place a record already uses stays listed, marked "(unpublished)" or "(trashed)", and a product price row for an unpublished country is kept, with a note that it is not used for storefront prices while the country is unpublished. The prices editor keeps a price row's unpublished currency selected and marked instead of showing another one. A customer whose saved address is in a country the shop no longer delivers to sees that country named, no country chosen, and a request to choose another one. The phone field keeps its full list of countries.

A visitor or a delivery address in an unpublished country, or in a town inside one, is priced as one with no country: that country's own price rows, discounts and taxes, and the taxes of a shipping charge delivered there, do not apply while it is unpublished. They are kept as they are, and publishing the country brings its prices back at once, with no rebuild.

Every gallery image gets a real thumbnail at the thumbnail size, whether it is uploaded or picked from the media library; until now an upload used its full image as its thumbnail. A new installation's thumbnail size is 500 x 500. An updated shop keeps the size stored in its Options: 200 x 200, 2.1's default, unless it was changed (Options can raise it to 500 x 500 before Recreate all thumbnails). Tools > Media gains Recreate all thumbnails (after changing the size) and Create missing thumbnails (only those that are missing, the full image, or smaller than the size allows), run in the background with their progress under Tools > Tasks and a report of the images whose file is missing; images given by a web address are left as they are. A thumbnail you pick yourself for an image from 2.2.0 on is left as it is by both. A thumbnail picked by hand before 2.2.0 is not known as picked (2.1 did not record it): Recreate all thumbnails makes it again from the image, like every other thumbnail (Create missing thumbnails too, when it is smaller than the size allows), and removes the earlier file from images/commerce (the shop's image folder) unless another image uses it. A merchant who kept a thumbnail of his own there picks it again afterwards, from his own copy. Any thumbnail made again replaces its earlier file, which is deleted unless another image uses it; a file outside the image folder is never deleted. An image too large to read in the memory a background run has is reported with that reason, and the run goes on with the next image.

Two gallery images no longer share one file: picking an image already in the gallery, or a thumbnail from it, makes its own copy, and deleting an image, a product or a Tools > Media selection removes only the files no other image uses. Before, deleting one product could delete another product's image. A second upload with the same file name no longer overwrites the first product's image when a media plugin saves images in another format (such as WebP).

A library image whose file name has a space can be picked; an image description longer than 75 characters no longer makes a gallery save fail (the field stops at 75, a longer one is shortened, and the API refuses it in plain words).

A background job whose work keeps ending the process before a step is done (for example at a PHP memory or time limit) no longer holds up the jobs after it: at the third attempt that has not finished a step it is marked failed with the error "Stopped after 3 runs that each ended before finishing a step, usually at the server's PHP memory or time limit. Raise the limit, then Retry.", and Tools > Tasks offers Retry and Mark resolved for it. A step that finishes starts the count again.

For plugins: a payment's or shipment's effect on the order now runs after the payment or shipment is saved and after the order's money lock is released. A gateway that saves a payment inside the order's money lock sees the order move only once its lock is released, not before its save returns. A refund that settles a payment in full marks that payment refunded the same way. Two payment changes made before either has moved the order (for example an authorization and its capture inside one lock) move the order once, to the status of the last one.

For developers: a shipping charge's tax chain now names the tax rule of each rate. ShippingCharge::$chain, CartTotals::shipmentCosts()['chain'], CartTotals::shipmentTaxChain(), PlacementCart::shipmentTaxChain() and Order::shipmentTaxChain() give each entry as ['rate' => '24', 'name' => 'VAT'] (before: the rate texts alone, ["10","5"]), and #__alfa_order_shipments.shipping_tax_chain, now a text column, stores the same entries as JSON, each name whole and in its own letters. A carrier that passes its own shipping_tax_chain to the shipment ledger hands each entry as a rate text or exactly that rate and name; anything else is refused. A chain stored before 2.2.0, its rates alone, is still read, as rates no rule is named for. The order line's tax name (#__alfa_order_items.tax_name) is text and kept whole, and core no longer calls OrderCreator::clampTaxName(), which stays a helper for a plugin's own column of 255 characters. Each document line keeps the tax name frozen at issue, whole, in #__alfa_document_items.tax_name.

For plugin and template developers: the items view announces every rendered result set (a page, a filter swap or a reloaded card) with the event onAlfaResultSetRender (group alfa-search), naming the engine and its attribution, so an engine loads its own scripts there; a template override cannot lose it. The filters module announces a swapped listing with the browser event alfa:results:updated on #alfa-app[data-view="items"], bubbling, after joomla:updated. A handle the engine marks as belonging to one response keeps that page out of Joomla's page cache, and the search endpoint then sends Cache-Control: no-store, private. A template override of com_alfa/items/default.php written before 2.2.0 renders no handle and no order until it calls the view's resultSetAttributes() on the results container; one of default_item.php written before 2.2.0 keeps printing its own data-position on every card, with a handle or without, until it calls the view's resultAttributes() instead.

For plugins: payment plugins have four new methods in the payment plugin base class: orderBalance() (the order's signed balance), countReferenceHolders() (how many of the gateway's own rows hold a provider reference), refundTypeFor() (whether a refund of one of its payments is full or partial) and claimPendingAttempt() (the gateway's one exclusive claim of a pending attempt for a provider reference; of two deliveries exactly one wins; a blank reference is refused, any other is stored byte for byte). The base class is the supported payment API: a gateway uses it and never calls the payment ledger or writes the payments table itself.

Payment and shipping plugins: a payment or parcel row written through the base class's builder records the plugin that wrote it; the method it names must be one of that plugin's, or the row is refused (a method whose type was changed no longer passes for another plugin's). getPaymentMethod() answers exactly the method asked, or the order's own method while the order records that plugin, and never another method of the same plugin. Two new base-class reads: findOwnRowByReference() (the one row of the gateway holding a provider reference) and firstMethodRow() (a method's first settled payment or refund). The bundled Standard payment and shipping methods act only on their own rows. A refund written through the builder records the method of the payment it returns; a reversal or chargeback recorded through the base class acts only on the plugin's own money. Every base-class door that updates or deletes a row (the builder's save, settleAttempt(), supersedeAttempt(), assignShipmentItems(), deletePayment(), deleteShipment()) acts only on the plugin's own rows, and a row keeps the plugin that wrote it: it may move to another method of that plugin, never to another plugin's.

For plugins: a plugin that handles Alfa events is a SubscriberInterface plugin and lists in getSubscribedEvents() every broadcast Alfa event it handles; the events Alfa addresses to it alone (a panel it owns, a tool it runs, clear data, cart charges and placement checks) go in the new TargetedHandlersInterface::getTargetedHandlers() and never in getSubscribedEvents(). Payment, shipping, item-field and search plugins inherit their declaration from their base class (TARGETED_EVENTS) and need no change; the base classes' subscriber maps now hold only broadcast events.

For plugins: every contribution names its plugin as group.element, the first argument of the event's typed method: columns()->column(), the row and bulk actions' action(), AdminListRowDataEvent::value() (replacing writes to rowData), AlfaAdminContext::append(), BuildMenuEvent::item(), add() and section(), GetAccessActionsEvent::action(), CartTotalsEvent::contribution() and the new addTotalAdjustment(), OrderPlaceValidateEvent::reject(), ItemDisplayEvent::addSurface() and CartItemDisplayEvent::addSurface() (replacing their slot methods), CollectCatalogProjectionsEvent::addProjection(). It is attribution, never an authorisation. Alfa no longer loads a contributing plugin's language; the plugin loads its own. CartContribution loses its source parameter: a cart charge is frozen with the source group.element.code.

For plugins: onCartTotals, onOrderPlaceValidate and onCartItemDisplay are delivered to the enabled alfa plugins the customer's access levels admit, in their order, each once, on one event for the whole cart, through each plugin's targeted declaration; a system plugin cannot add charges or refuse a placement. onAlfaSearchInputLayout is delivered to the configured search engine's plugin only.

For plugins: AlfaAdminContext's row data and markup are read through rowData(), rowValues() and html(); value() and append() are the only ways to write them, so nothing enters without its plugin. Core's menu entries and headings arrive with the onAlfaBuildMenu event, and BuildMenuEvent::section() takes the plugin placing the heading first. The answering() method of the customer-context events is Alfa's: a plugin never calls it.

For plugins: Alfa Commerce reaches Joomla's plugin system through one helper, AlfaPluginHelper (administrator/src/Plugin): broadcasts on the shared dispatcher, and targeted calls to one selected plugin, which is never booted while disabled. Anything that leaves a targeted handler is that handler's failure. A plugin whose import failed in a request takes no part in it, logged as a warning. The developer manual describes both modes, the two declarations and the identity rule.

For plugins: cards, setup checks, tools, document type providers, stock allocation providers and search engines name their plugin as group.element: CollectCardsEvent::addCard(string $contributor, DashboardSurface $surface, string $id, string $title) replaces on(), and top(), metrics(), main(), side() and bottom() take (string $contributor, string $id, string $title); CollectSetupChecksEvent::add(string $contributor, string $id, string $label); GetToolActionsEvent::add(string $contributor, string $id, string $label) and addAction(string $contributor, PluginAction $action), with addFromArray() and setActions() gone; addProvider() and addEngine() take group.element in place of the extension name. A provider's document types are kept under plg_{group}_{element}; a provider whose earlier builds passed another name moves its stored types itself in its own update (core adds no alias). Core's setup checks enter the event through its constructor, and every typed method requires its contributor. attributeTo() is gone. The six events reach every plugin that listens, whatever its group.

For plugins: a panel's events, onExecuteToolAction, onClearData and an item field's hooks reach the one plugin they are for through its targeted declaration (TargetedHandlersInterface, or its family's TARGETED_EVENTS) and never through getSubscribedEvents(). A tool runs only on the plugin it is listed under, and its entry (label, card, enabled and mutating flags) is that plugin's own answer to onGetToolActions; a claim made in its name by another plugin and not confirmed by it is dropped and logged. A panel save, delete or task addressed to a plugin without a handler for it is an error staff see. A disabled item-field plugin is no longer booted. Clear Data may run a plugin's onClearData while the plugin is disabled (under the lock of Clear everything, with its name, group and params).

For plugins: a plugin of a group Joomla loads itself (task, system, user, content and the others) declares its targeted handlers with a public getTargetedHandlers() alone and names no Alfa Commerce class or interface at class level, so it still loads when Alfa Commerce is uninstalled; a plugin of the alfa groups implements TargetedHandlersInterface. A dashboard card whose data throws stays hidden and is now logged at WARNING with its plugin, its id and the error, once per request.

For plugins: a dashboard card whose data callback answers an empty array has nothing to show and is no longer drawn, so it is no longer logged as a layout that drew nothing; a card with no data callback is drawn as before. AdminCard gains live(): a live card is resolved on every request, never from the dashboard's cache, for content that changes while the shop works.

For templates and developers: the cart totals are the new overridable layout cart.summary (html/layouts/com_alfa/cart/summary.php), which receives prepared rows. A template override of com_alfa/cart/default_cart_items.php keeps the old table footer and English phone labels until it is updated; an override of com_alfa/cart/default_cart_empty.php shows the notice only with the element marked data-cart-changed-notice, and styles it only under an element of class com-alfa (the layout's root since 2.2.0): an override that keeps its own bare root shows the notice unstyled on a fresh empty page. The table rules under .com-alfa weigh one class more than before, so a template rule on Alfa Commerce's own table cells may need one class more to win. COM_ALFA_CART_COUPON_REMOVE now takes the code as %s: an override that prints it with Text::_ shows the placeholder, and should use Text::sprintf with the code. The task cart.sections answers GET only (any other method: 405) and is never cached. One public storefront event, alfa:cart:changed (on document, detail {source, action}), follows each successful change of the cart's contents; a script that shows the cart listens to it and reads its own endpoint again. alfaProductAdded and alfaCartMethodsRefreshed keep their meaning. The cart module's global variable modAlfaCartTogglerCounterValue is removed: the counter mode is the toggler's data-counter-mode attribute; an override of the module's layout without it keeps the counter it printed until it is updated.

For templates: an override of com_alfa/cart/default_order_completed.php reads the order from the view's confirmation value (OrderConfirmation) instead of the view's orderNumber, customerEmail and hasDownloads, which are removed; until it is updated it shows nothing of the order. The page's script and stylesheet are the asset com_alfa.order-completed. Note that the web server's access log records the page's address, key included, as it records the web cron's.

For developers: the catalogue's price data (the REST API's catalogue payload, PriceResult::toArray() and formatAll()) states every saving and discount figure on one basis, tax excluded, and says so: savings.basis and discounts.basis are "tax_excluded", and discounts.total is the same figure as savings.total_amount. For a discount applied after tax, savings.total_amount, savings.price_amount and discounts.total are now the net amount (10,00 in the example above) where 2.1.4 gave the discount stage's tax-included 12,40; before tax nothing changes. A rule's own fixed amount (discounts.applied[].amount) is the rule's term and names the basis it is stated on in amount.basis: "tax_excluded" for a rule applied before tax, "tax_included" for one applied after it. The search payload carries no saving amount; its percent is unchanged.

For plugin developers: the stored price index announces what changed with the event onAlfaPricesChanged, after the commit and once per write: the products whose stored prices changed, why (a product, a discount, a tax, a category, a manufacturer, a customer group set being prepared, or a rebuild) with its id, the customer group sets written, and each changed row with its old and new final price (a new row has no old price, a removed one no new price). A system plugin or an alfa plugin hears it by listing the event in its subscriber map. A window that opens by itself, the prices the product page and the cart compute live, whether a place may buy, the rows of a deleted place (the administrator's delete event tells of the place) and those of a customer group set nobody holds any more are not announced. A write that changes more than 5,000 rows outside a transaction of its caller is announced by several events as its parts commit, each exact for its rows; inside the caller's transaction its rows wait for the commit. A listener's own price write raises its own event, heard after the one it is handling. With no listener the index reads nothing more than before.

note.item: Quality and reliability release: user-reported fixes, safer order processing, reliable after-save work, and notifications in each administrator's language.

It updates an installed shop of 2.0.0 or later in place: Joomla runs its database changes automatically (schema 2.1.4: two new tables for tasks, and five new columns in the notifications table). Requirements are unchanged.

fix.item: On a Joomla installed in a subfolder (for example example.com/shop/), Select from library now opens the media library instead of a Not Found page, on items, categories, manufacturers, a variant's gallery and the thumbnail buttons, so an image can be chosen and saved. On such a site a picked image's preview also shows at once, the Email preview and Send test email windows are styled, phone fields show their country flags, and a customer whose order, payment or shipment return can no longer be identified is sent to the shop's home page instead of the domain's.

When the server refuses Generate combinations, Add options, Add values or a visibility rule (for example while the item itself still holds stock), the window now shows the reason and nothing is created. Before, Generate combinations said that every combination already existed, and the others said nothing.
Saving a document series as the default makes it the only default of its document type: the type's previous default series is no longer left default too.

On MySQL 8.0, a shop with a single customer group that has its own prices showed that group's customers the public price on the item listing, because each customer's pricing groups were read wrongly. They are now read the same way on MySQL and MariaDB, and the listing shows the group's price.

On the orders list, the first amount is what the shop holds now: completed payments less refunds and chargebacks, so the held amount and the Due line always add up to the order total. Before, a partly refunded order still showed the whole amount paid. The Partial badge and its bar follow the held amount, and a Chargeback line shows under the amount when the bank took money back, like the Refunded line. Every amount ever paid stays in the order's payments.

The order screens show a shipment's status, an order line's shipping state, a payment's transaction status and refund type, and each History action in the administrator's language instead of its stored English code (for example pending or shipped). A value Alfa Commerce does not know is shown as stored. The two tab titles of the guide under Tools > GitHub - Commit and Pull Request are translated too.

A fresh installation over a leftover administrator/components/com_alfa or components/com_alfa folder, with no record of Alfa Commerce in Joomla, now installs normally instead of stopping with a database error. An installation that stopped that way earlier completes when it is run again.

Every plugin and module included with Alfa Commerce shows its full, real date in Extensions: Manage. Six showed 1970-01-01 (Country, Text, Textarea, Console Alfa Inventory, the scheduled task for the list prices of customer groups, and Standard payment), and seven showed only a year and a month, or a day without its leading zero (the Choice and Tel form fields, the Choice item field, Standard shipping, and the Filters, Cart and Search modules).
The notice that a content language still lacks translations clears itself when that content language is deleted. If it was deleted outside Content Languages, the next language update clears it.

When an order's history entry cannot be saved, the danger notification about it stays until an administrator dismisses it, and it is raised again when another entry of that order is lost; a later entry no longer withdraws it.

A document issued for an order withdraws only the automatic-issue notifications it answers: those about its own type and the general one. A delivery note no longer withdraws the invoice's notification about a missing tax number or a failed invoice.

addition.item: Follow-up work triggered by a saved change, such as an e-mail, a plugin reaction or a document, is recorded together with the change. If the change fails, that work is discarded with it; if the change succeeds, the work is kept and runs immediately after the save. If the request stops first, the work is not lost: it runs later when an administrator's notification bell refreshes, or from Tools > Tasks > Run outstanding tasks.

Work that failed before it took effect is tried again automatically after 1 minute, 5 minutes, 30 minutes, 2 hours, 6 hours and 24 hours. Work that failed for good, or whose outcome cannot be known, is never repeated by itself: a notification says so, and Tools > Tasks lists each one with Resend, Run again or Mark resolved. Every attempt and every decision is recorded with the task.

Notifications read in the language of the administrator who reads them, in the notification bell and under Notifications: an administrator working in Greek reads a notification in Greek, one working in English reads the same notification in English. Each notification also keeps its text as it was first written, in the shop's default administrator language; that text is shown when the extension that raised the notification is no longer installed, and it never changes afterwards. Searching the notifications finds them by that text and by the values they name, such as an order number. During the update, notifications written before 2.1.4 are given their language keys where their text is recognised; the update's message counts them, and the others are shown as they were written.
Installing a language pack warns when Joomla's own language of the same name is not installed on the site, and says where to install it.

change.item: On the orders list, the order number opens the order (its hint says Open order), and a Quick view button under it unfolds the order's read-only summary: items, shipments, payments, discount codes and notes. Its arrow turns while the summary is open. The separate arrow column is gone, so the list is narrower, and the orders guided tour points at the new button.

Everything triggered by an order's status change after it is saved (the stock movement, the download access, the documents, the status e-mail and the plugins' reaction) is recorded with the change and runs right after the save, in that order. A completed payment's download access and documents, and a new order's confirmation e-mail, are recorded the same way. When the request stops after the save, this work runs later instead of being lost.

The status e-mail and the order confirmation e-mail record each recipient's outcome. A recipient whose message was rejected before hand-off, or rejected by the mail server, is retried automatically. A message that was handed over but produced no definite outcome may already have arrived, so it is never sent again automatically. Tools > Tasks offers Resend, which sends only to the recipients not recorded as sent. An order's e-mails go out in the order its statuses were entered. With Send Mail switched off in Joomla's Global Configuration, an order's e-mail fails at once and is never sent later by itself; Resend sends it once mail is on.

An order's History tab records an e-mail that failed, is held or was resent, a plugin reaction that failed, is held or was run again, and a task marked resolved, with who did it and, for Mark resolved, why. Each such record reads in the language of the administrator who reads it.

A notification raised while a change is being saved (low stock, a backorder, a stock movement that failed, an automatic document that could not be issued, a lost history entry, a payment's report and every other) is written as soon as the save is committed, never inside the save itself: staff reading or dismissing notifications no longer wait for that work, and a database deadlock on a notification can no longer undo the change. Notifications of the same subject are written in the order they were raised, so an older one never overwrites a newer one (a low stock warning written after the item was restocked, for example). A notification of a change that fails is never written, and none is written twice.

Work deferred while a payment's money lock or a shipment's booking lock is held now waits until the lock is released, so a slow mail server or plugin no longer keeps a second payment or booking action on that order refused as busy.

An automatic document that could not be issued because the database was briefly busy (a deadlock or a lock wait) is tried again automatically. A document the shop's settings refuse (no series, a missing tax number) still raises its own notification and is not retried.

Uninstalling Alfa Commerce also removes its installed Alfa Commerce language packs, through Joomla's installer, and names each pack it removed. Joomla's own language packages and other extensions are not affected. When a pack is uninstalled but some of its files cannot be removed (in a folder that cannot be written, for example), a message says so and asks for the remaining files to be removed by hand, and the maintenance log lists them. A pack that cannot be uninstalled is named, with the advice to uninstall it in System > Manage > Extensions. A pack whose package manifest is missing is named in a message of its own, because Joomla cannot uninstall it without that manifest either.

After an Alfa Commerce language pack is installed or updated, Alfa Commerce updates its language tables itself, so the order statuses and system fields it created get their names in the new language. While Alfa Commerce is in maintenance after an unfinished Clear everything, this waits for Clear everything.

The warnings shown while the System - Alfa Commerce Sync plugin is disabled or not installed also say that a language pack installed meanwhile names the order statuses and system fields only after Language tables is run under Tools > Database Sync.
Removing a language folder from inside Alfa Commerce's own folders is reported in a message of its own, naming each folder and its number of files.
Every plugin and module included with Alfa Commerce carries the Alfa Commerce version, 2.1.4, in Extensions: Manage. The included libraries keep their own versions.

For plugins: onAlfaAdminAfterSave, onAlfaAdminAfterDelete and Joomla's onContentAfterSave and onContentAfterDelete are dispatched once the change is committed and Alfa Commerce's locks are released, never for a change that was undone, so a listener sees the record as saved and no longer runs inside the save: orders, items, categories, manufacturers, places, item fields and stock locations alike. The listeners that can refuse a deletion (onAlfaAdminBeforeDelete and Joomla's onContentBeforeDelete) are asked before the record is locked.

For plugins: onOrderStatusChange is dispatched right after the order's save is committed, after the stock movement, the download access, the documents and the status e-mail, and the listener sees the order as saved. A listener that fails is recorded with its task, and an administrator can run it again from Tools > Tasks.

For plugins: a notification is stored as a language key with its parameters and shown in each reader's language. NotificationHelper::push() accepts a NotificationText for the title and the message (NotificationText::from() names the extension whose language files hold the key) and still accepts literal text, which is shown as written to every reader. The event of onAlfaNotificationPushed gains titleKey(), messageKey(), arguments() and textDomain(); title() and message() return the text as first written in the shop's default administrator language, and group() returns a group key, such as COM_ALFA_NOTIFY_GROUP_ORDERS, for core's notifications.
For plugins: onAlfaNotificationPushed is dispatched for a notification raised during a save only once the whole save, its payment steps included, is finished, and never for a change that was undone.
For language pack authors: a pack's install script no longer has to update Alfa Commerce's language tables; Alfa Commerce does it after the pack is installed or updated.
For developers: the category options of the Items batch dialog and of the cart rule conditions come from one place, CategoryPickerPolicy. What they show is unchanged.

note.item: Maintenance release for 2.1.1 that changes where Alfa Commerce's language files are and how they load. It updates an installed shop of 2.0.0 or later in place, with no change to the database: the schema stays 2.1.1, so data kept after uninstalling 2.1.1 reconnects to a fresh 2.1.2 installation. Requirements are unchanged.

change.item: Every language file of Alfa Commerce is in Joomla's own language folders: administrator/language/<tag>/ for the component, its guided tours and its plugins, language/<tag>/ for the shop and its modules. The component keeps no language folder of its own.

The texts of the 33 guided tours are one file per language, com_alfa.tours.ini, beside com_alfa.ini and com_alfa.sys.ini; the 66 files of one tour each are gone. The tours' titles show in the header's tour menu on every administrator page, in Guided Tours and while a tour runs, in the administrator's language.

While the System - Alfa Commerce Sync plugin is disabled or not installed, every Alfa Commerce administrator page warns that Alfa Commerce needs it: without it the guided tours show language keys and Alfa Commerce no longer follows Joomla's users and user groups. A user who may manage plugins gets a link that opens the plugin. Installing or updating Alfa Commerce enables it again.

The installation and the update remove a language folder inside the component's own folders (administrator/components/com_alfa/language/ and components/com_alfa/language/) with everything in it, and name each one with its number of files. Nothing outside those two folders is touched.
A Greek file of Alfa Commerce 2.1.0 that the shop changed in Joomla's language folders is still kept and named by the update, as in 2.1.1.
Tools > Security reports a language file inside Alfa Commerce's own folders as an extra file, like any other file the release does not list.
The export of GitHub - Commit & Pull Request carries every file of the folders the manifests declare; no file is left out for its language any more.

For language pack authors: a pack for 2.1.2 has, for its language, com_alfa.ini, com_alfa.sys.ini, com_alfa.tours.ini and each plugin's two files in administrator/language/<tag>/, and com_alfa.ini and each module's two files in language/<tag>/: 38 files.

note.item: Maintenance release for 2.1.0. It updates an installed shop of 2.0.0 or later in place: Joomla runs its database changes automatically (schema 2.1.1: every Alfa Commerce table now uses one collation, utf8mb4_unicode_ci). Requirements are unchanged.

After updating: if System - Page Cache is enabled, clear Joomla's cache (System > Clear Cache), or pages cached by 2.1.0 keep their blank untranslated names; rebuild the index of a search engine so it carries the names as shown.
